exposure: Trial of labor (TOL) after one or two previous cesarean deliveries (CD)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (one minute APGAR score, neonatal care unit admissions, and mechanical ventilation rates)
cohort: Parturients attempting a TOL after one or two previous CDs at a single tertiary center, between 2005 and 2019
finding: While vaginal delivery rates were high in both groups, TOL after two previous CDs was associated with a lower vaginal delivery rate compared to TOL after one previous CD (83.1% vs. 88.5%, p < 0.01), but similar rates of uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Neonatal outcomes were less favorable following two CDs, but after adjusting for confounders, no independent association was found between neonatal composite outcome and TOL following two CDs.
